text:
maria: heads-up — staging started seeing intermittent DNS NX / timeouts after the heartbeat-prober rollout around 03:18. dig shows 200–500ms and occasional SERVFAILs. Not full outage but spikes affecting model fetches. anyone seen this?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: heartbeat-prober v2.3 -> staging @ 2025-11-12T03:18:40Z :white_check_mark:

ashok: ack. can you paste a sample /etc/resolv.conf from an affected pod and a failing dig ?

maria: sure, from pod gpu-infer-7c8b (staging):
```
# /etc/resolv.conf
search staging.internal svc.cluster.local svc.localcompany.com very.long.search.list.example.com
nameserver 10.12.0.10
options ndots:5 timeout:2 attempts:2
```

and dig output (same pod):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> model-registry.internal +time=2 +retry=1
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 3421
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; WARNING: got SERVFAIL
;; Query time: 432 msec
```

ben: interesting — ndots:5 + very long search list will cause extra suffix attempts per lookup. that multiplies queries per client. if egress NAT ports are limited we can hit 1:many ratio and drop responses. did conntrack or egress metrics spike?

priya: also watch for stub resolver handoff behavior — some libc resolvers will open multiple parallel queries (one for the absolute name plus suffixes) which we saw before with ndots high. combined with heartbeat-prober making aggressive probes could make bursts.

nate: pinging the egress LB / NAT allocs — looking at conntrack counters now.

nate: quick check: `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` -> 64532 (socket-heavy), `sudo conntrack -S | grep expect` shows a jump in udp entries around 03:20.

ashok: can you also check kube-proxy conntrack and ephemeral port usage on a node? I suspect source port exhaustion -> UDP drops (no retry) -> SERVFAIL on client.

maria: rolling a quick change: reducing ndots to 1 in staging ConfigMap for a subset of pods to see behavior. also restarted nscd/systemd-resolved on two effected pods.

priya: nice, if that moves the needle it’s likely query amplification. also let's capture packet traces for a pod (tcpdump udp port 53) to confirm missing responses vs server SERVFAILs.

maria: after ndots=1 change on 4 pods: 2/4 showed immediate improvement, query latencies down to ~40–60ms and no SERVFAIL for 15m. other 2 pods still sporadic.

ben: that matches a partial mitigation. still want to confirm egress NAT port pool and whether NAT rotation changed after patch. heartbeat-prober v2.3 added parallelism for health checks, might be creating many short-lived outbound sockets.

nate: found this in node kernel log around 03:19 -> `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` — that’s our smoking gun.

maria: paused heartbeat-prober rollout in staging and reverted to v2.2 for now.

priya: follow-ups: 1) add an alert on nf_conntrack table fill / conntrack drops, 2) instrument egress ephemeral port utilization per node, 3) cap heartbeat-prober probe parallelism and add jitter, 4) recommend lowering ndots/search length for workloads that do lots of short name lookups.

ashok: +1 to all. also add an egress-lb health check for TCP fallback path; we saw earlier that UDP truncated/resets cause longer degradations.

maria: thanks — creating an infra ticket to track fixes and a retro for the rollout change. will paste ticket link when done. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy paused: heartbeat-prober rollback -> v2.2 applied to staging @ 2025-11-12T03:35:05Z

ben: small immediate action for app teams: set `options ndots:1` in pod DNSPolicy / ConfigMap for high-chatty services until infra fixes are in.

maria: noted. thanks everyone. will follow up with packet captures + ticket.

priya: adding one more note — we should consider making ndots/ search list warnings part of our preflight linter when creating k8s services across many zones. repeated search suffixes are the hidden multiplier. :eyes:
